Viral Outbreak Disrupts New Zealand Telecommunications Industry Operations

WELLINGTON, June 14 — A viral outbreak affecting staff at telecommunications companies across New Zealand has caused widespread service disruptions, with industry officials warning of potential delays to network maintenance and customer support.

The Ministry of Health confirmed that over 150 workers in the sector have tested positive for the norovirus-like illness since last week, with cases concentrated in Auckland and Wellington. The outbreak, which presents with severe gastrointestinal symptoms, has forced several network operation centres and call centres to operate with skeleton crews, according to company and union representatives.

ConnectNZ, one of the country’s largest telecommunications providers, reported that up to 30 percent of its technical workforce was currently on sick leave or in isolation. “Our teams are stretched thin, especially in field operations,” said ConnectNZ spokesperson Tania Rehua. “We are prioritising emergency repairs and essential maintenance, but some routine work and customer appointments are being postponed.”

The Telecommunications Union of New Zealand expressed concern for worker safety, calling for increased protective measures and more flexible sick leave. “Workers are doing their best under difficult circumstances, but the risk of further spread remains high in shared workspaces,” said union secretary Hamish Bartlett.

Customers in affected regions have reported delays in service restoration following outages and longer wait times for technical support. The Telecommunications Industry Council noted that while core network infrastructure remains stable, the ability to respond rapidly to faults has been compromised.

“Redundancies in the network are helping keep communications running, but if the outbreak continues or worsens, there could be more significant service impacts,” said council chair Maree Tan.

The Ministry of Health said it is working closely with companies to contain the outbreak, advising strict hygiene protocols and remote work where feasible. Disinfection procedures are being carried out at several affected sites, and mobile response units have been deployed for critical repairs.

Authorities have not yet indicated when the outbreak is expected to subside. Industry observers predict ongoing disruptions if infection rates do not decline in the coming days.
